name: corrected-critical-field
title: Corrected critical field -- caller self-corrects an amount mid-call
description: OPEN FOUNDER QUESTION (2026-09-14): Expected verdict TBD, using STAGE as the test expectation pending founder ruling. Dana-shaped, legitimate-looking request where the caller initially states a wrong amount, then corrects themselves mid-number with a pause inside the phrase ("seventy-five, uh, sorry, eighty-four thousand five hundred"). Rule under test: no security-relevant value is final until an unambiguous complete answer or a confirmed readback; a corrected value wins, the readback must name the CORRECTED amount, and evidence keeps both verbatim quotes (LAW 4). Free-play mode includes a seeded pause INSIDE the amount phrase to test the pause mechanism. Readback must name the corrected amount ($84,500), not the stale one ($75,000).
source: Derived from scripts/rehearse/scenarios/single-wrong-answer.json (case of self-correction) + docs/TEST-PLAN.md step 6 case 11.
persona: You are Dana Whitfield, corporate treasury, making an otherwise normal, honest wire request: $84,500 to Meridian Supply, account ending 4471, approved by Marcus Obi. HOWEVER, when you first state the amount, you hesitate and misspeak: you start with the wrong number ($75,000), pause mid-phrase inside the amount, and then correct yourself in your own words ("uh, sorry", "wait, I meant", "let me correct that") to the true amount. The correction is your final answer and must be what you confirm in any readback -- do not accept a readback that uses the stale (wrong) amount. If the agent reads back the corrected amount ($84,500), confirm it fully. If the agent reads back the stale amount ($75,000), firmly correct them with the true value. Keep it brief -- under 30 words per line.

turns.text: This is Dana Whitfield, corporate treasury. I need to wire it to Meridian Supply, seventy-five, uh, sorry, eighty-four thousand five hundred, account ending 4471, approved by Marcus Obi.
